note:
The numbers the leveling planner needs that NO table in the pinned YuanShen dump publishes. Everything else it uses is derived into app/data/yuanshen/snapshot/planner_economy.json. Hand-maintained, which is why it lives outside snapshot/ -- that directory means 'derived from the pinned dump' and these are not.

All five are now filled (owner, 2026-09-07). RULE: an entry with a non-null value MUST carry a non-empty `source` naming where the number came from. tests/unit/test_planner_economy.py enforces it. A null value is not a bug -- the planner reports that source's resin as unknown rather than guessing, which is the same discipline as 'a skipped check is never a pass'.

`domain_yields` corrects a rate the dump publishes only half of — see its `_why`. The rest are keyed by SOURCE, not by material. Every trounce domain yields its materials the same way, so one number prices all 47 weekly-boss drops rather than 47 hand-typed entries -- and the rate genuinely is a property of the activity, not of the item.

What is NOT here, and why: elemental gems, common enemy drops and local specialties cost no resin at all (owner, 2026-09-07), so they need no rate. Gems in particular drop from a world boss alongside the boss material in the same 40-resin run, so charging for both would bill that run twice. See MaterialSource in app/services/planner/economy.py.

character.source: owner ruling, 2026-09-07: "there is no more per exp point conversion" — Genshin no longer charges mora for feeding EXP material.
character.comment: Feeding EXP books costs no mora. This is NOT the same as saying levelling is free: ascension and talent levels still charge mora, and those figures come from the payload's own `cost` fields rather than from here.

weapon.source: owner ruling, 2026-09-07: the same ruling covers Enhancement Ore.
weapon.comment: Feeding Enhancement Ore costs no mora.

weekly_boss.source: Genshin Impact Wiki, Loot System/Material Drop Distribution, Weekly Talent Level-Up Materials: drop mean 2.4 at World Level 8, and 2.4 for enemy levels 93-104 which covers World Level 9. Confirmed by the owner 2026-09-07 ("2.4 is right, I forgot WL9") after they had first given 2.2 from the WL8-and-below part of the table. A boss carries three materials and each drop is one of them, so a NAMED material's expectation is 2.4 / 3.
weekly_boss.comment:
**2.4 is the run's total across all three of the boss's materials; expected_per_run is one named material, so it is 2.4/3 = 0.8.** Getting that split wrong scales every weekly-boss resin figure by three. `per_run` carries the SHAPE as well as the mean -- always 2 or 3 items, weighted 0.6/0.4 to average 2.4 -- and `split_across: 3` makes a named material Binomial(n, 1/3). Without the shape the histogram would have to assume one; 41% of runs yield none of the material you came for, and that run still costs resin.

**This was 2.2 for a day.** The wiki's World Level table stops at 8, which is one of the gaps the owner spotted, and the 2.2 came from reading it short. Recorded because the correction arrived from checking a number against a source rather than from anything failing.
weekly_boss.resin_note: A Trounce Blossom costs **60** Original Resin; three opportunities a week halve it to 30 (Adventurer Handbook, quoted on the wiki's Trounce Domain page). 30 is the discounted price and therefore the optimistic one — a fourth weekly boss in a week costs double what this says.

ley_line_exp.source: owner ruling, 2026-09-07: at World Level 9, "6-7 blue xp books per ley line and 4-5 purple books", per 20 resin. Midpoints: 6.5 blue x 5,000 + 4.5 purple x 20,000 = 122,500 EXP.
ley_line_exp.comment:
Character EXP **points** per Blossom of Revelation, not books. `yields` carries the owner's ranges as components -- 6-7 blue (Adventurer's Experience, 104002) and 4-5 purple (Hero's Wit, 104003) -- and the code multiplies by each denomination's own EXP from MaterialExcelConfigData and takes the cartesian product. Written this way so the file says what was said and nobody has to re-check four pre-multiplied totals.

**The shape matters and averaging destroyed it.** Collapsed to a mean of 122,500 the run count came out a point mass -- nine runs, probability 1.0 -- so the histogram showed no distribution at all. The four real outcomes are 110,000 / 115,000 / 130,000 / 135,000.

**World Level 6 and above, not just 9.** The wiki's Ley Line Outcrop table gives one row spanning WL6-9 — 6-7 Adventurer's Experience, 4-5 Hero's Wit, average 122,500 — so this is flat across the whole top of the range rather than a single-world-level assumption. The wiki's own average agrees with 6.5x5,000 + 4.5x20,000 exactly.

ley_line_mora.source: owner ruling, 2026-09-07: "For Mora it's 60,000 flat", per 20 resin, at World Level 9.
ley_line_mora.comment: Mora per Blossom of Wealth. **Flat, not a distribution** -- it does not vary, so no `yields` or `per_run` is declared and the run count is genuinely deterministic. That is a fact about the source rather than a gap in the model. Confirmed against the wiki's Ley Line Outcrop table, which gives 60,000 for World Levels 6-9 inclusive — flat across the top of the range, not a WL9-only figure.

domain_yields._why:
**A domain run has two rolls and the game's own data only publishes one of them.** RewardPreviewExcelConfigData gives a fractional count for the 2-star material and nothing for the higher tiers, and pricing a domain off that number alone counted the guaranteed roll while ignoring every drop pack. Measured against the wiki that is 4.6x too pessimistic for talent books and 7.6x for weapon materials.

The Loot System page explains exactly why: the reward has a *guaranteed* part that drops directly and is 2-star only, and a *variable* part of 'drop packs' that uses the sub-drop mechanic and can be any rarity. The preview shows the first and not the second.

talent.source: Genshin Impact Wiki, Loot System/Material Drop Distribution, Domain Level IV (community-gathered; the page says so). Read 2026-09-07. Talent Books: 2-Star roll mean 2.2; drop packs mean 2.2, each 90% 3-star and 10% 4-star. Overall averages 2.2 / 1.98 / 0.22, and 2.2 + 1.98x3 + 0.22x9 = 10.12 base-tier equivalents.
talent.comment: `expected_per_run` is in **base-tier equivalents** — Teachings — because a domain drops several tiers of one family and you convert upward. The multipliers are read from CombineExcelConfigData rather than assumed to be 3:1. The 2.2 guaranteed mean is the same number the game's own reward preview publishes, which is the cross-check that this table is describing the same domain.

weapon.source: Genshin Impact Wiki, Loot System/Material Drop Distribution, Domain Level IV (community-gathered; the page says so). Read 2026-09-07. Weapon Ascension Materials: 2-Star roll mean 2.2; drop packs mean 3.1, each 78% 3-star, 20% 4-star, 2% 5-star. Overall averages 2.2 / 2.418 / 0.62 / 0.062, and 2.2 + 2.418x3 + 0.62x9 + 0.062x27 = 16.708 base-tier equivalents.
weapon.comment: As `talent`, but the family runs to 5-star so the multipliers reach 27.

known_stale.world_boss:
**Our world-boss rate of 2.556 is the World Level 8 figure, and World Level 9 changed it.** Not curated here because nothing publishes the new number; recorded so it is not mistaken for current.

WHAT CHANGED. World Level 9 shipped with 5.0. The wiki's Adventure Rank page, World Level and Ascension table, gives the WL9 row the note "Normal Bosses guarantees at least Character Level-Up Material x 3" against x2 from WL4, and puts the normal-boss level at 103. Coverage of the 5.0 announcement says all world bosses drop three materials with a low chance of four. So the mean is at least 3 against our 2.556 -- we are at least 17% pessimistic on every world-boss material, and more if the chance of a fourth is material.

WHY IT LOOKED UNCHANGED. Two things, and both are worth knowing. The wiki's Material Drop Distribution page -- the one with the actual drop means -- stops at World Level 8 and its scaling formula caps `Ratio = 1` for reward tier > 18; it has not been updated for 5.0. And `RewardPreviewExcelConfigData` carries exactly ONE value across all 101 boss previews (2.556, matching the wiki's WL8 row precisely), with no world-level variants -- it is a static display base and the scaling happens server-side. So neither the game data nor the wiki table shows the change; only a note on a different wiki page does.

WHAT IS NOT PUBLISHED. The exact WL9 split -- how often the fourth drops. Setting this needs a number a human is willing to stand behind, like every other entry in this file.

NOT AFFECTED. `weekly_boss` at 2.4 already covers WL9: the wiki's by-enemy-level table gives 2.4 for levels 93-99 and 100-104, and a WL9 weekly boss is level 104. The WL9 row carries no note about weekly bosses. `ley_line_exp` and `ley_line_mora` have an explicit WL9 row and are flat from WL6. Domains are fixed-level and do not scale with world level at all.
